applies_why: The judge text labels a Matthew 1:20 issue UNDERDETERMINED and gives reasons, so the rule governing grounds for UNDERDETERMINED applies.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: For 'single verse does not state': (1) it forbids grounding UNDERDETERMINED on a verse's silence about a link or its contrary; (2) it does not forbid grounding on the verse's own words stating the source. The judge's text cites the verse's own words stating the source, so it falls under reading (2).
why: The judge did not say Matthew 1:20 fails to state the link or contrary; it said the sentence's own words state the source, so K-S2's prohibition on using a single verse's non-statement is not breached.
